title: GitHub’s model for secret detection: Finding more secrets with less noise
author: Batu Ozturkler
description: GitHub’s context-aware secret classifier improves detection quality, raises weighted acceptance by 11.5%, and reduces median scan execution time by 86%. The post GitHub’s model for secret detection: Finding more secrets with less noise appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
summary: 11.5% higher acceptance Owner-weighted alert precision 86% lower median scan execution time Post-push scanning 98% lower serving cost Compact model vs. remote LLM calls Secret scanning works best when developers are confident in the findings. Catch too little, and real credentials can remain in a repository.
takeaways: Because the model is small and efficient to run on our inference infrastructure, it costs much less to serve and is simpler to scale than an LLM-based pipeline.

To address this challenge, we trained a secret classifier specifically for GitHub’s product needs: distinguishing real credentials from lookalikes while meeting the speed and efficiency requirements of scanning at scale.
Context-aware classification : A fine-tuned ModernBERT classifier evaluates each candidate and its surrounding context.
